page: Vultr vx1-m-64c-512gb is a memory-optimized cloud server instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include any GPUs and is provisioned with 1 GB of network-attached local storage, meaning primary storage requirements must be met via external network volumes.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier memory and processing capabilities. Large-block memory bandwidth tests show read speeds of 532.73 GB/sec and write speeds of 251.91 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% of tested hardware. The AMD EPYC processor delivers a PassMark CPU score of 98,920.13 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3,710.38. Multi-threaded performance is also robust, as evidenced by a bzip3 decompression speed of 550.47 GB/sec and a PassMark database operations score of 42,060.8, both ranking in the top 10%.

The primary tradeoff of the vx1-m-64c-512gb is its minimal 1 GB network-attached local storage and the absence of a dedicated GPU, which limits its utility for heavy local disk-I/O operations or hardware-accelerated graphics tasks without external attachments. However, its high memory-to-vCPU ratio offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads by reducing the need to over-provision CPU cores simply to acquire sufficient RAM. This profile is highly suitable for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, multi-threaded data decompression, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
